rationale: Machine amplifies thoughts to link minds in a shared duel, loosely evoking a shared simulated space; but it is telepathic amplification, not a networked text game like MUD1.
Spoken reports are quickly 'audioscribed' into text, matching the function of dictation transcription; no mechanism is given and it is 1953 prior to 1990 Dragon Dictate.
A giant tank displaying exact positions of every enemy unit matches live situation display of tracked objects; fed by scouts and 3D rather than radar-computer consoles, mechanism vague.
Turnstile checks money and pass and locks if phony, loosely like machine-read access cards, but the passage centres on currency/pass validation and is unspecific about identity encoding.
Mentions computer time consumed by including each satellite in takeoff problems, ground trajectory calculation; the milestone is an onboard computer doing orbital maneuvers, so only loosely related.
Main and auxiliary ship computers fail to fix position after a Jump; navigation computers are implied but the quote only shows them unable to work, and the Jump context is fictional.
Cockpit crowded with monitor screens of an astrogation computer matches an onboard navigation computer in function; no calculation mechanism of orbital burns is described.
Command-centre world and space map displays with coloured symbols match a computerized situation display in function; the quote does not say live radar tracking or computer driving.
A coin-operated machine dispenses a map of a level on request, loosely information retrieval, but no search over large records or queries is described.

A table-map where red circles automatically show positions of all air-cities closely matches an automatically updated tracked-object display; sensors and computer not specified, context is air-cities.
A stenoreel recorded dictation and switches to transcriber mode, matching dictation-to-text function; the recognition mechanism is not described, and it predates the 1990 product.
A mechanical educator with headset teaches visitors, but it transfers knowledge directly rather than presenting lessons, tests and grading as in CAI.
Electronic digital computer digests binary digits and outputs flight coordinates, matching navigation calculation; it computes for interstellar flight and does not steer or perform burns.
Onboard electronic computer works out course corrections for capture by Mars' gravity, close to onboard computer orbital maneuver computation; Mars capture context differs.
A boxed 'Socialization Kit' with a manual for building artificial companions evokes companion robots only as a kit, with no mechanism or function visible in the quote.

A tiny metal proxy controlled remotely to explore small scales loosely evokes microscopic machines; the real milestone is molecular shuttles and the quote's proxy is merely small, not molecular or in the body.
'She was just a thing' says nothing about conversation in natural language; the quote alone does not describe the function.
A sensipsych machine teaches skills via vivid experiences, similar to training aids but lacking lessons, tests and grading of CAI; experiential simulation rather than instruction.
A machine with only two neuron-equivalents behaves lifelike, hinting at neuron-like units, but no learning or interconnected computation resembling a neural net trained by backpropagation.
A master computer on loan from M.I.T. is described only physically; the claim of natural-language question answering is not in the quote, so function match is weak.
A temple electrode wired to a pocket device points toward brain monitoring, but nothing says it reads thoughts or images, versus fMRI image reconstruction.
A ship brain is told what to remember and does so; this is spoken programming of a machine's memory, loosely like voice command but speech recognition is not clearly shown.
Eye-reflection tracking speaks the word being read for language learning, a teaching aid with no lessons, tests or grading as in CAI.
A governor's fingers on a computer keyboard beside his chair suggest personal desk computing, but the quote gives nothing on ownership or size, and hardly a mechanism.
Sense tapes feed a prisoner an imagination-shaped simulated experience, matching immersive VR in function; the mechanism is dream-machine tapes and the context is prison conformity testing.
An interpreter hears questions and answers from a large microtape memory, which is speech understanding in spirit; the quote frames it as pre-recorded automation, not recognizing spoken commands.
Comptometer-regulated trajectory means calculating machines regulating a ship's trajectory, matching onboard navigation computation in function; vague on mechanism.
Z9M9Z is said to be far better than other command methods, evoking a fleet coordination computer, but the quote gives no analysis of battle data or planning mechanism.
A shipboard machine speaks with a person and admits it is a machine, hinting at conversation, but the quote shows no understanding of questions in ordinary language beyond a bare statement.
A mechanical educator teaches a foreign language, an instructional machine loosely like CAI, but no lessons, testing or grading is described.
A housecleaning robot with hose and mops appears, but no spoken command or recognition appears in the quote itself.
Humanoid servant robots controlled by the computing sections of a master machine matches central computer directing many robots in function; the Kiva warehouse system is much narrower in context.
Artificial near-living things resembling pets, but the quote says only they are near-living; a toy dog on a leash is a distant analogue.
One cannot compute an orbit without another reference point, which matches orbit calculation function; no onboard steering or mechanism and from observations rather than a computer.
A dictator device takes a spoken message, which is voice recording with a binding gift; the quote gives no transcription to text, so only partial.
Telemanipulators move people around, matching remote manipulation by operators in function; the quote has no mention of operator viewing and used for prisoners, not nuclear handling.
A machine does in fifteen minutes what takes a man six hours of brain work, aboard a ship approach calculation; matches the function with no mechanism.

A quick computation on a planetary calculator then firing steering rockets to set an arching course matches calculating a course and executing burns; calculator is not shown to command the burn itself.

A desk-cabinet card-file system holding over three million items and returning an item plus near-items in three seconds matches record retrieval in seconds well, though it is card-based and personal-sized rather than networked.
An android made with all the abilities of the original William Norden is a robot copy of a specific person in function; looks and mechanism not described, and it thinks faster.
Machines sense each person's wrist-band and sort them to levels, tracking identity and location via a worn device; the real milestone is offender ankle monitors reporting to a receiver.
A logic computer used to compute truth hints at answering questions, but the quote has no natural-language interface or broad knowledge base.
A Central File machine intelligence directing robots to destroy organic life matches a central computer coordinating many robots; context is war, not warehouse logistics.
A pocket device showing animated figures in garments is a small display of moving images, loosely like a computer screen, but not a computer showing data.
Shipboard computer banks automatically compensate course and power against gravitational tides, matching an onboard system that computes and steers; mechanism is relays and a fictional force.
A slate changes colour and shows lines of text at a button press, closely matching a portable reader displaying text; storage of books is not explicit.
Flashes from a small tube held to the eyes for identification match eye scan identification closely; the quote doesn't say retina patterns are compared.
A huge three-dimensional chart of a star system with fleets matches a volumetric display in function; it is not described as holographic and tracks fleets, versus a moving hologram.

Electronic brains inserted in the human brain and connected to main neural paths match a neural implant linked into the nervous system; the cochlear implant is a restorative sensory device, which differs in context.
Machinery handles electrical equipment with no one driving it, matching an unattended plant in function; the quote covers unloading and assembly with no maintenance or self-running factory described.
Doors open at a wave of a hand, matching gesture control of a machine in function; the real milestone is a touch panel and no sensing mechanism is described.
Card-sorting analyzer with slots and pointer for criminal records loosely evokes analysing records, but is mechanical sorting rather than a computerized wanted-persons database.
A voice-writer producing clear script directly matches a machine turning speech into written text; recognition mechanism not stated and context differs from DOS product.
A computer that 'knows what it is talking about' and advises is only asserted knowledgeable; no questions in ordinary language or broad knowledge is shown.
Friends who always stay with you suggests artificial companions only by implication; the quote shows no robot function or mechanism.
Punching a designation on a keyboard and instantly getting the record on a screen matches interactive database retrieval well; scale of collection and search by query terms are not shown.
A million-plug board around a tank is a control and communication panel, loosely tied to a plotting display, but nothing says it shows live positions.

A computer was consulted and predicts winning the war against aliens, matching outcome calculation in function; no data analysis mechanism and the SAGE milestone was air defence, not strategy forecasting.
Police reading a suspect's memories via psyching, requiring a court order, matches reading specific memories from the brain in function; the mechanism is unspecified.
Directors of incredible machinery controlling robots point to remote direction, but there is no manipulator or sensor feedback described.
A poetry machine emitting output matches machines producing creative work in function; the quote is a bare mention, with no mechanism, and about poetry rather than music.
Computers that are electronic analogues of living brains match brain-modelled machines in function; the quote offers no neuron-like units, learning or training mechanism.
A thinkwriter that records the reporter's text sits somewhat near thought-to-text, but the quote shows only him sitting at it, with no thought decoding stated.
An Information Center that can answer any human question matches question answering in function; operated by video booths and human or robot staff, so not a computer in ordinary language.
Circuits imitating one function of nerve tissue in light-seeking robots evoke neuron emulation loosely, but are a simple analogue circuit not an interconnected learning network.
A commander who is a remote-controlled android operated by its ruler is teleoperation of a body rather than an exact double of a specific person, though it stands in for the ruler.
A robot's optical scanner reads a citizen's classification card and acknowledges, matching a machine reading cards for access; punched-hole card context differs.
A gate opens when the winning ticket is fed into a slot, a machine reading a token for access; it checks a number rather than a person's identity, mechanism not specified.
Synaptic cells summing, integrating, cancelling and comparing before passing findings on closely echo neuron-like units; no learning is stated and the pipeline is coded tape processing.
An alien machine that extracts language, thoughts and name from a person's mind matches reading thoughts in function; no mechanism and goes beyond images.
A character dictates a full account, and the quote gives only dictation with no sign of recognition or transcription, so function hardly stated beyond dictation.
An artificial brain with mechanical glands and pumped fluids copies the human brain physically, not as interconnected computing units; points toward brain modelling loosely.
Two minds think a world into shape together, sharing a virtual world by function; but only two people, shaped by thought, with no network or machines described.
A shipboard library of question-and-answer tapes designed to answer almost any question matches retrieval in function; tape-based, and the search mechanism is unspecified.
A handful of brain cells piloting the Skylark better than a human matches a device steering a spacecraft in function; mechanism is an organic brain, and not orbital calculation.
A machine that reads typewriting on cards with no punching matches optical character reading closely; the insurance claim context differs from mail sorting.
A computer given legs walks around, loosely a remote-controlled body; the quote itself says it walks under its own effort, so teleoperation is not present.
Thought as a tangible force in a place, lights and machines responding, evokes thought control loosely; no brain signal link or device is stated.
An elevator takes a rider to a floor when given a name, a spoken command carried out; the quote says only 'gave it' the name, so voice is inferred.
A robot sees far beyond human vision, a sense of sight, whereas the milestone is a machine hearing digits; the sense and the mechanism differ.
Electronic puppets imitating animals are remote-controlled decoys, loosely like machine animals but not pets or toys.

A police computer sorting characteristics of all known criminals in its memory to find suspects closely matches a computerized criminal database used for identification; predictive analysis is absent.
Feeding numbers to calculators over charts for navigation matches calculating courses in function; no steering, and quote hardly indicates orbits.
Fully automatic Lensmakers requiring neither maintenance nor attention match a self-running plant in function; the product is a mystical device and no mechanism is given.

Circuitry duplicated in units so tiny that connecting wires are the problem matches microminiaturized circuits in function and the wiring bottleneck; the mechanism is organic molecular rather than solid-state.
Portable mass-production factories turning out a complete ship every eleven seconds match automated production; they are operated and not shown to maintain themselves, with fantastic transmutation.
A table voice announces the menu and politely replies to a spoken order, matching spoken ordering; recognition itself is only implied.
A translator machine speaks aloud, speeds the words to human tempo and imitates mannerisms, matching generated speech output; it converts alien speech and it is not reading text.
Idle giant robots with a human's mind inhabiting them match remote operation by a person in function; the quote itself only shows robots standing idle, and mind transfer differs from manipulators.
Detectors in cars pick up a person's pattern, hinting at brain detection, but identify who rather than read thoughts or images.
Robot control via a bow antenna with radio blocked by the hull is radio control of robots in passing; no operator seeing through sensors and no manipulation described.
One commander presses fleet-control keys to run the fleet, matching central direction of many units; keyboard rather than computer and ships not robots.
Dictating to a steno-robot that produces a message matches dictation in function; the quote shows no transcribing mechanism.
Alien computers found at other star systems and used for astrogation hint at navigation computers, but they are found artefacts, and the quote describes only size.
A machine working out a supply list and holding records matches record handling loosely; the quote shows planning rather than query and fast retrieval.
Personality traits thumbed in for a companion, cheerful and submissive, match a made companion with selectable character; physical/affective design missing and not commercial toy.
Needles in wrists with tubes linking a person to Brain One to punch data match a direct human-computer link; it is a wired invasive interface, not clearly brain signals controlling a device.
Brushing the hand across a screen to switch machinery on and off matches touch-panel control closely; the context is alien machinery rather than answering questions.
A huge machine said to be the most developed in the world, underground, for defence; the quote shows no scientific calculation, only prestige.
Robots fixed up with sound receptors and a voice match hearing and speaking robots in function; nothing about recognizing or following commands.

A surgically placed device detecting nerve impulses of tongue, lips and larynx to reconstruct speech is a body-linked electronics device, but it is a speech-output prosthesis and not a sensory implant for hearing.
A vast electronic brain computing orbits of artificial moons and keeping beams linked to them matches orbit calculation; it is ground-based and tracks satellites rather than guiding a ship.
A robot ticket clerk's camera records each traveller's face for files, closely matching cameras capturing faces for identification; matching against stored images is not stated.
Hunting in reference tapes and finding an explicit collection on the needed subject matches retrieval by subject; scale and speed are unspecified and tape-based.
A robot postal station whose sorter swallows ten thousand letters matches an unattended automated facility; it describes mail sorting rather than a self-maintaining plant.
Automatic equipment designed to do practically everything for the navigator matches onboard automated navigation in function; no orbital calculation or burns specified.
Odal is suddenly enveloped in darkness and finds himself in a spacesuit, a convincing machine-generated experience, matching immersive VR in function; mechanism is telepathic amplification.
A machine tuning in to thought waves like a television tunes pictures matches reading thoughts directly from the brain in function; the actual image reconstruction is not shown.
Checkpoint machines probing a man's inner thoughts to find spies match reading thoughts in function; the mechanism is vague and the context is security screening.
A cybernetic cooker in the kitchen suggests an automatic appliance, partly matching a home run by machines; it is one appliance named only, with no response to occupants shown.
Information from a mind through helmet pickups translated into English by a machine matches thought-to-text in function and sensing path; the mechanism of decoding is not described.
Searching the Archives for a man's past and present records matches retrieval over stored files in function; speed and query mechanism are not stated.
Circuits laid out for a robot bedbug point to an insect-like machine, but it is only a passing reference and not a toy or pet.
An idealizator that makes thoughts visible as images on a mirror matches displaying mental images in function; the mechanism is psychons-to-quanta and not decoding brain signals.
A machine that identifies alien visitors and gives orders is a recognition and command machine, not one answering arbitrary questions in ordinary language.
Equipment automated to perfection with redundant channels taking over on component failure matches a self-running unmanned station in function; no factory or maintenance described.

A master computer directing fleets and setting optimum maneuvers, trusted by statesmen, matches a computer planning operations and war outcomes; SAGE was air-defence and not strategy planning, so context differs.
Washing machines with built-in voices announce status, a machine with a speaking voice; the mechanism of synthesis is not stated and the quote only says they have voices.
A door opens when the tenant says his name and an elevator fails to respond to 'Seventh Floor', closely matching voice-operated doors and machines; the recognition fails in the elevator case.
A stroboscope on a blind man's head extracting information is loosely brain reading, but flickering light stimulation does not read specific thoughts or images.
A humanoid robot built to give pleasure with memorized erotic books is a companion robot for sex; the quote reveals no sensor mechanism and the milestone is a robot dog.
SRB machines integrating data to show a statistical ratio of winning the war close match calculating war outcomes; the SAGE air-defence milestone was a different task.
An electromechanical educator named only, with no description of lessons, tests or grading; it evokes a teaching machine loosely.
Robots with eye-lenses and ear-drums who stop and call for help when blinded and deafened have senses; the milestone is spoken-digit recognition and the quote shows sensors only in passing.
An asteroid computator with radar set-up that protects a ship matches radar-linked automatic avoidance computation; an on-board computer but obstacle avoidance and not orbital maneuvering.
Robots automatically controlled by radio from the camp computer as their brain closely match a central computer directing many robots; a camp rather than warehouse context.
The quote says only that the machine is the largest in the world; the robot-control function comes from the summary, so function is not visible in the quotation.
Saying 'Open' to a lock and the device recognizing him and letting him in closely matches voice-operated door; speaker recognition is also implied, but the apricot milestone was a computer.
A voco-typer used to produce articles by voice closely matches a voice-to-text machine; the recognition mechanism isn't described.
Running all robberies for a period through the computer matches a police computer analysing records for patterns; the NCIC was a lookup database, not pattern analysis.
A spaceship brain plots a one-gee orbit on a spoken order and handles take-off, matching onboard orbit calculation closely; the spoken command and Phobos context differ.
Directing the Cow through a vocoder panel to take over control of equipment matches voice commands to a computer in function; the quote shows only commands and no recognition.
Workers' nerves becoming cooperative with cybernetic machines through practice evokes a human-machine link, but no signal reading or device control is stated.
A computer scanning for loose equipment or left-behind personnel is a ship monitoring function, not orbital calculation or steering.
An advertisement for revealing innermost thoughts is only a claim; no machine mechanism and probably entertainment.
Dreams appearing visibly with adventures before the mind's eye matches an immersive generated world in function; the quote is fantastic and does not describe machine feeding of senses.
A telepath instrument could tell where the pet was hidden, matching reading hidden thoughts in function; but the quote says telepath rather than machine and has no mechanism.
An android that changes before his eyes drawing on his mind hints at reading desires, but the quote shows only a changing figure.
Selection depending on what you wished is vague; question answering over encyclopedias is only in the summary, not in the quotation.
Extracting yards of paper from a drawer suggests a delivered record but the quote shows no stored-collection search or query.
A keyboard-operated electric reckoner performing complex calculations in seconds is a desk machine; it matches arithmetic on demand but not a small battery-powered personal device.
The quotation is about a being that checked everything within limits and never erred; it says nothing about chess or a computer program playing it.
Apparatus responding to his thoughts from a distance matches devices controlled by thought alone; the mechanism and the implant are unspecified.
A building of machinery taking in news, indexing it by category and filing it matches stored-record indexing and retrieval; querying and speed are not shown.
The Menograph or mind-writer by name suggests writing thoughts down; the quote is a bare name with no mechanism.
A speculative artificial man assembled from camera eyes, telephone ears and dynamo head points to a humanoid machine; it is a rhetorical question without walking, talking or handling.
A three-dimensional map hanging in the air matches volumetric mid-air display in function; the mechanism of projection is unknown.
Thinking at an instrument to command remote ships matches a device controlled by thought; mechanical beings and radiated thought, with no signal reading described.
Android female surrogates manufactured and shipped to colonists clearly match sex robots in function; manufacture and usage differ from a robotic pet milestone.
A door mike following with its snout and a hi-fi picking a random tape evoke responsive household devices, but no recognition of spoken words is shown.
